import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Bombieri–Lang conjecture

The Bombieri–Lang conjecture predicts that the $K$-rational points of a positive-dimensional
variety of general type over a number field $K$ are not Zariski dense.

Mathlib has no notion of canonical bundle or Kodaira dimension, so this file defines "general
type" from scratch, following the classical description of pluricanonical forms as rational
differential forms. For an integral scheme $X$ over $K$ with function field $F = K(X)$, an
$m$-canonical rational form of degree $n$ is an element of
$(\bigwedge^n_F \Omega_{F/K})^{\otimes m}$. Such a form is regular on a nonempty affine open
$U = \operatorname{Spec} A$ if it is an $A$-linear combination of forms
$(df_{1,1} \wedge \dots \wedge df_{1,n}) \otimes \dots \otimes
(df_{m,1} \wedge \dots \wedge df_{m,n})$
with all $f_{i,j} \in A$. When $X$ is smooth of dimension $n$ over $K$, the forms regular on
every nonempty affine open are exactly the global sections $H^0(X, \omega_X^{\otimes m})$ of the
$m$-th power of the canonical bundle, and their $K$-dimension is the $m$-th plurigenus $P_m(X)$.
A smooth proper variety of dimension $n$ is of general type if its Kodaira dimension is $n$, i.e.
$P_m(X)$ grows like $m^n$. Kodaira dimension is a birational invariant of smooth proper
varieties, and a general variety is of general type if some (equivalently, every) smooth proper
variety birational to it is.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Bombieri–Lang conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombieri%E2%80%93Lang_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Kodaira dimension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kodaira_dimension)
- [La74] S. Lang, *Higher dimensional diophantine problems*, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 80 (1974),
  779–787.
- [Po12] B. Poonen, *Uniform boundedness of rational points and preperiodic points*,
  [arXiv:1206.7104](https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.7104).
- [DT15] P. Das, A. Turchet, *Rational Points, Rational Curves, and Entire Holomorphic Curves on
  Projective Varieties*, Contemp. Math. 654 (2015),
  [arXiv:1407.7750](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.7750).
-/
namespace BombieriLangConjecture
open CategoryTheory AlgebraicGeometry Filter
open scoped TensorProduct
universe u
variable (K : Type u) [Field K]

noncomputable scoped instance functionFieldAlgebra (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))]
    [IsIntegral X] : Algebra K X.functionField :=
  haveI : Nonempty (⊤ : X.Opens) := ⟨⟨genericPoint X, trivial⟩⟩
  ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of K)).inv ≫ (X ↘ Spec (.of K)).appTop ≫
    X.germToFunctionField ⊤).hom.toAlgebra
blocks.docstring:
The `K`-algebra structure on the function field $K(X)$ of an integral scheme `X` over
`Spec K`, induced by the structure morphism `X ⟶ Spec K`.

justification.name: BombieriLangConjecture.functionFieldAlgebra
justification.why_needed: Scoped instance giving the K-algebra structure on the function field of an integral scheme over Spec K (needed to form Ω[K(X)⁄K]). Mathlib only provides Algebra Γ(X, U) X.functionField, not an algebra structure over the base field of a K-scheme.

blocks.code:
abbrev RationalPluricanonicalForm (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
    (n m : ℕ) : Type u :=
  ⨂[X.functionField]^m (⋀[X.functionField]^n Ω[X.functionField⁄K])
blocks.docstring:
The `K`-vector space $(\bigwedge^n_{K(X)} \Omega_{K(X)/K})^{\otimes m}$ of rational
`m`-canonical forms of degree `n` on an integral scheme `X` over `Spec K`, where $K(X)$ is
the function field of `X`. When `X` is smooth of dimension `n` over `K`, this is the generic
fibre of the `m`-th tensor power $\omega_X^{\otimes m}$ of the canonical bundle.

justification.closest_existing_considered: KaehlerDifferential, exteriorPower, TensorPower (used as building blocks); no scheme-level Ω_{X/S} exists
justification.name: BombieriLangConjecture.RationalPluricanonicalForm
justification.why_needed: The space (⋀ⁿ_{K(X)} Ω_{K(X)/K})^{⊗m} of rational m-canonical forms; Mathlib has no sheaf of differentials or canonical bundle on schemes.

blocks.name: RationalPluricanonicalForm
blocks.text:
/-- The `K`-vector space $(\bigwedge^n_{K(X)} \Omega_{K(X)/K})^{\otimes m}$ of rational
`m`-canonical forms of degree `n` on an integral scheme `X` over `Spec K`, where $K(X)$ is
the function field of `X`. When `X` is smooth of dimension `n` over `K`, this is the generic
fibre of the `m`-th tensor power $\omega_X^{\otimes m}$ of the canonical bundle. -/
abbrev RationalPluricanonicalForm (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
    (n m : ℕ) : Type u :=
  ⨂[X.functionField]^m (⋀[X.functionField]^n Ω[X.functionField⁄K])

blocks.code:
noncomputable def regularPluricanonicalForms (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))]
    [IsIntegral X] (n m : ℕ) (U : X.Opens) [Nonempty U] :
    Submodule K (RationalPluricanonicalForm K X n m) :=
  Submodule.span K {ω | ∃ (a : Γ(X, U)) (f : Fin m → Fin n → Γ(X, U)),
    ω = algebraMap Γ(X, U) X.functionField a •
      ⨂ₜ[X.functionField] i, exteriorPower.ιMulti X.functionField n fun j ↦
        KaehlerDifferential.D K X.functionField (algebraMap Γ(X, U) X.functionField (f i j))}
blocks.docstring:
The rational `m`-canonical forms of degree `n` on an integral scheme `X` over `Spec K`
that are *regular* on the nonempty open `U`, meaning that they are
$\Gamma(X, U)$-linear combinations of forms
$(df_{1,1} \wedge \dots \wedge df_{1,n}) \otimes \dots \otimes
(df_{m,1} \wedge \dots \wedge df_{m,n})$ with all $f_{i,j} \in \Gamma(X, U)$.
Since $K$ maps into $\Gamma(X, U)$, this $\Gamma(X, U)$-span is the same as the `K`-span of
the forms $a \cdot (df_{1,1} \wedge \dots \wedge df_{1,n}) \otimes \dots$ with
$a, f_{i,j} \in \Gamma(X, U)$.

This description is the correct one when `U` is affine and `X` is smooth of dimension `n`
over `K`: then it is the space of sections of $\omega_X^{\otimes m}$ over `U`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: SheafOfModules / IsVectorBundleWithRank (no canonical bundle instance available)
justification.name: BombieriLangConjecture.regularPluricanonicalForms
justification.why_needed: Sections of ω^{⊗m} over a nonempty (affine) open U, as the K-span of forms a·(df₁₁∧…∧df₁ₙ)⊗…⊗(dfₘ₁∧…∧dfₘₙ) with a, f_{ij} ∈ Γ(X, U) inside the generic fibre; no Mathlib notion of sections of a canonical bundle.

blocks.name: regularPluricanonicalForms
blocks.text:
/-- The rational `m`-canonical forms of degree `n` on an integral scheme `X` over `Spec K`
that are *regular* on the nonempty open `U`, meaning that they are
$\Gamma(X, U)$-linear combinations of forms
$(df_{1,1} \wedge \dots \wedge df_{1,n}) \otimes \dots \otimes
(df_{m,1} \wedge \dots \wedge df_{m,n})$ with all $f_{i,j} \in \Gamma(X, U)$.
Since $K$ maps into $\Gamma(X, U)$, this $\Gamma(X, U)$-span is the same as the `K`-span of
the forms $a \cdot (df_{1,1} \wedge \dots \wedge df_{1,n}) \otimes \dots$ with
$a, f_{i,j} \in \Gamma(X, U)$.

This description is the correct one when `U` is affine and `X` is smooth of dimension `n`
over `K`: then it is the space of sections of $\omega_X^{\otimes m}$ over `U`. -/
noncomputable def regularPluricanonicalForms (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))]
    [IsIntegral X] (n m : ℕ) (U : X.Opens) [Nonempty U] :
    Submodule K (RationalPluricanonicalForm K X n m) :=
  Submodule.span K {ω | ∃ (a : Γ(X, U)) (f : Fin m → Fin n → Γ(X, U)),
    ω = algebraMap Γ(X, U) X.functionField a •
      ⨂ₜ[X.functionField] i, exteriorPower.ιMulti X.functionField n fun j ↦
        KaehlerDifferential.D K X.functionField (algebraMap Γ(X, U) X.functionField (f i j))}

blocks.code:
noncomputable def globalPluricanonicalForms (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))]
    [IsIntegral X] (n m : ℕ) : Submodule K (RationalPluricanonicalForm K X n m) :=
  ⨅ (U : X.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen U) (_ : Nonempty U), regularPluricanonicalForms K X n m U
blocks.docstring:
The rational `m`-canonical forms of degree `n` on an integral scheme `X` over `Spec K`
that are regular on every nonempty affine open of `X`. When `X` is smooth of dimension `n`
over `K`, this is the space of global sections $H^0(X, \omega_X^{\otimes m})$ of the `m`-th
tensor power of the canonical bundle $\omega_X = \bigwedge^n \Omega_{X/K}$.

justification.name: BombieriLangConjecture.globalPluricanonicalForms
justification.why_needed: H⁰(X, ω_X^{⊗m}) as the intersection of the regular forms over all nonempty affine opens.

blocks.name: globalPluricanonicalForms
blocks.text:
/-- The rational `m`-canonical forms of degree `n` on an integral scheme `X` over `Spec K`
that are regular on every nonempty affine open of `X`. When `X` is smooth of dimension `n`
over `K`, this is the space of global sections $H^0(X, \omega_X^{\otimes m})$ of the `m`-th
tensor power of the canonical bundle $\omega_X = \bigwedge^n \Omega_{X/K}$. -/
noncomputable def globalPluricanonicalForms (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))]
    [IsIntegral X] (n m : ℕ) : Submodule K (RationalPluricanonicalForm K X n m) :=
  ⨅ (U : X.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen U) (_ : Nonempty U), regularPluricanonicalForms K X n m U

blocks.code:
noncomputable def plurigenus (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
    (n m : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Module.finrank K (globalPluricanonicalForms K X n m)
blocks.docstring:
The `m`-th *plurigenus* $P_m(X) = \dim_K H^0(X, \omega_X^{\otimes m})$ of an integral
scheme `X` over `Spec K`, computed with forms of degree `n`. This is the classical plurigenus
when `X` is smooth and proper of dimension `n` over `K` (in which case
$H^0(X, \omega_X^{\otimes m})$ is finite-dimensional).

justification.name: BombieriLangConjecture.plurigenus
justification.why_needed: P_m(X) = dim_K H⁰(X, ω_X^{⊗m}); needed to express Kodaira dimension.

blocks.name: plurigenus
blocks.text:
/-- The `m`-th *plurigenus* $P_m(X) = \dim_K H^0(X, \omega_X^{\otimes m})$ of an integral
scheme `X` over `Spec K`, computed with forms of degree `n`. This is the classical plurigenus
when `X` is smooth and proper of dimension `n` over `K` (in which case
$H^0(X, \omega_X^{\otimes m})$ is finite-dimensional). -/
noncomputable def plurigenus (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
    (n m : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Module.finrank K (globalPluricanonicalForms K X n m)

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 14]
lemma globalPluricanonicalForms_le (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
    (n m : ℕ) (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) [Nonempty U] :
    globalPluricanonicalForms K X n m ≤ regularPluricanonicalForms K X n m U :=
  iInf_le_of_le U (iInf_le_of_le hU (iInf_le _ ‹_›))
blocks.docstring: A form that is regular on every nonempty affine open is regular on each of them.
blocks.name: globalPluricanonicalForms_le
blocks.text:
/-- A form that is regular on every nonempty affine open is regular on each of them. -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
lemma globalPluricanonicalForms_le (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
    (n m : ℕ) (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) [Nonempty U] :
    globalPluricanonicalForms K X n m ≤ regularPluricanonicalForms K X n m U :=
  iInf_le_of_le U (iInf_le_of_le hU (iInf_le _ ‹_›))

blocks.code:
def IsBirational (X Y : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of K))] : Prop :=
  ∃ (U : X.Opens) (V : Y.Opens) (e : (U : Scheme.{u}) ≅ V),
    Dense (U : Set X) ∧ Dense (V : Set Y) ∧
    (e.hom ≫ (V.ι ≫ (Y ↘ Spec (.of K)))) = (U.ι ≫ (X ↘ Spec (.of K)))
blocks.docstring:
Two schemes `X` and `Y` over `Spec K` are *birational* over `K` if they contain dense open
subschemes that are isomorphic as `K`-schemes.

justification.closest_existing_considered: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.RationalMap / PartialMap (no notion of birational equivalence or inverse)
justification.name: BombieriLangConjecture.IsBirational
justification.why_needed: Birational equivalence over K (isomorphic dense open subschemes over Spec K), needed to define general type for arbitrary varieties via smooth proper models. Mathlib has RationalMap but no birationality predicate.

blocks.name: IsBirational
blocks.text:
/-- Two schemes `X` and `Y` over `Spec K` are *birational* over `K` if they contain dense open
subschemes that are isomorphic as `K`-schemes. -/
def IsBirational (X Y : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of K))] : Prop :=
  ∃ (U : X.Opens) (V : Y.Opens) (e : (U : Scheme.{u}) ≅ V),
    Dense (U : Set X) ∧ Dense (V : Set Y) ∧
    (e.hom ≫ (V.ι ≫ (Y ↘ Spec (.of K)))) = (U.ι ≫ (X ↘ Spec (.of K)))

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 14]
lemma isBirational_refl (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))] : IsBirational K X X :=
  ⟨⊤, ⊤, Iso.refl _, by simp, by simp, by simp⟩
blocks.docstring: Every scheme over `Spec K` is birational to itself.

blocks.code:
def IsSmoothProperOfGeneralType (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
    (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  IsProper (X ↘ Spec (.of K)) ∧ IsSmoothOfRelativeDimension n (X ↘ Spec (.of K)) ∧
    ∃ c : ℕ, 0 < c ∧ ∃ᶠ m in atTop, m ^ n ≤ c * plurigenus K X n m
blocks.docstring:
A smooth proper integral scheme `X` of dimension `n` over `Spec K` is *of general type* if
its Kodaira dimension $\kappa(X)$ equals `n`, i.e. if its plurigenera $P_m(X)$ grow like
$m^n$: there is a constant $c > 0$ with $m^n \le c \cdot P_m(X)$ for infinitely many `m`.

(By Iitaka's theorem, $P_m(X) = O(m^{\kappa(X)})$, and $P_m(X) \ge a m^{\kappa(X)}$ for all
large `m` in the semigroup of `m` with $P_m(X) \ne 0$, so this is equivalent to
$\kappa(X) = n$.)

justification.name: BombieriLangConjecture.IsSmoothProperOfGeneralType
justification.why_needed: A smooth proper integral K-scheme of relative dimension n with Kodaira dimension n, i.e. plurigenera growing like m^n.

blocks.name: IsSmoothProperOfGeneralType
blocks.text:
/-- A smooth proper integral scheme `X` of dimension `n` over `Spec K` is *of general type* if
its Kodaira dimension $\kappa(X)$ equals `n`, i.e. if its plurigenera $P_m(X)$ grow like
$m^n$: there is a constant $c > 0$ with $m^n \le c \cdot P_m(X)$ for infinitely many `m`.

(By Iitaka's theorem, $P_m(X) = O(m^{\kappa(X)})$, and $P_m(X) \ge a m^{\kappa(X)}$ for all
large `m` in the semigroup of `m` with $P_m(X) \ne 0$, so this is equivalent to
$\kappa(X) = n$.) -/
def IsSmoothProperOfGeneralType (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
    (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  IsProper (X ↘ Spec (.of K)) ∧ IsSmoothOfRelativeDimension n (X ↘ Spec (.of K)) ∧
    ∃ c : ℕ, 0 < c ∧ ∃ᶠ m in atTop, m ^ n ≤ c * plurigenus K X n m

blocks.docstring:
An integral scheme `X` over `Spec K` is *of general type* if it is birational over `K` to
a smooth proper integral `K`-scheme `X'` of some dimension `n` with Kodaira dimension
$\kappa(X') = n$. Since the Kodaira dimension is a birational invariant of smooth proper
varieties, the choice of `X'` does not matter.

justification.name: BombieriLangConjecture.IsGeneralType
justification.why_needed: A K-scheme is of general type if it is birational over K to a smooth proper integral K-scheme of general type (the standard birationally invariant definition).

blocks.name: IsGeneralType
blocks.text:
/-- An integral scheme `X` over `Spec K` is *of general type* if it is birational over `K` to
a smooth proper integral `K`-scheme `X'` of some dimension `n` with Kodaira dimension
$\kappa(X') = n$. Since the Kodaira dimension is a birational invariant of smooth proper
varieties, the choice of `X'` does not matter. -/
def IsGeneralType (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))] : Prop :=
  ∃ (X' : Scheme.{u}) (_ : X'.Over (Spec (.of K))) (_ : IsIntegral X') (n : ℕ),
    IsBirational K X X' ∧ IsSmoothProperOfGeneralType K X' n

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 14]
lemma IsSmoothProperOfGeneralType.isGeneralType (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))]
    [IsIntegral X] {n : ℕ} (hX : IsSmoothProperOfGeneralType K X n) : IsGeneralType K X :=
  ⟨X, inferInstance, inferInstance, n, isBirational_refl K X, hX⟩
blocks.docstring:
A smooth proper integral `K`-scheme with Kodaira dimension equal to its dimension is of
general type.

    [IsIntegral X] {n : ℕ} (hX : IsSmoothProperOfGeneralType K X n) : IsGeneralType K X :=

blocks.code:
def rationalPoints (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))] : Set X :=
  {x | ∃ p : Spec (.of K) ⟶ X, (p ≫ (X ↘ Spec (.of K))) = 𝟙 _ ∧ p.base default = x}
blocks.docstring:
The set of `K`-rational points of a scheme `X` over `Spec K`, viewed as a subset of the
underlying (Zariski) topological space of `X`: the images of the `K`-morphisms
`Spec K ⟶ X`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Hom-sets Spec (.of K) ⟶ X and Scheme.Hom.IsOver (used to build the set); no existing 'set of rational points' definition
justification.name: BombieriLangConjecture.rationalPoints
justification.why_needed: The set of K-rational points of a K-scheme as a subset of its underlying Zariski space, so that Zariski density can be expressed with Mathlib's Dense.

blocks.code:
@[category research open, AMS 11 14]
theorem bombieri_lang_conjecture [NumberField K] (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))]
    [IsIntegral X] [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of K))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of K))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of K))] (hdim : 0 < topologicalKrullDim X)
    (hX : IsGeneralType K X) :
    ¬ Dense (rationalPoints K X) := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Bombieri–Lang conjecture.** Let $K$ be a number field and let $X$ be a positive-dimensional
variety (an integral separated scheme of finite type over $K$) of general type over $K$. Then
the set $X(K)$ of $K$-rational points of $X$ is not dense in the Zariski topology on $X$.

The positive-dimensionality hypothesis excludes the point $\operatorname{Spec} K$, which is of
general type with trivially dense rational points.
blocks.name: bombieri_lang_conjecture
blocks.text:
/-- **Bombieri–Lang conjecture.** Let $K$ be a number field and let $X$ be a positive-dimensional
variety (an integral separated scheme of finite type over $K$) of general type over $K$. Then
the set $X(K)$ of $K$-rational points of $X$ is not dense in the Zariski topology on $X$.

The positive-dimensionality hypothesis excludes the point $\operatorname{Spec} K$, which is of
general type with trivially dense rational points. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11 14]
theorem bombieri_lang_conjecture [NumberField K] (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))]
    [IsIntegral X] [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of K))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of K))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of K))] (hdim : 0 < topologicalKrullDim X)
    (hX : IsGeneralType K X) :
    ¬ Dense (rationalPoints K X) := by
  sorry
end BombieriLangConjecture

claims.decomposer_note: Implicit universal quantifiers over every number field K and every (geometrically integral, projective) variety X of general type over K, with X required positive-dimensional (per the article's 'general form'; a 0-dimensional point is of general type with trivially dense rational points), the density being of X(K) in X's own Zariski topology; 'general type' (Kodaira dimension = dim X) has no Mathlib definition and needs a bespoke one, and the article-only 'weak' surface form and 'refined' finiteness-on-an-open-subset form are not posed by the statement.
claims.reviewer_why: c06's declaration (with my edits: added a proven `rationalPoints_spec` test, tidied references, wrapped long lines) is the cleanest faithful statement. It quantifies over every number field K (same universe as the scheme) and every integral, separated, finite-type K-scheme X with 0 < topologicalKrullDim X that is of general type, and asserts ¬ Dense (rationalPoints K X) in X's own Zariski topology, with rational points = images of K-sections Spec K ⟶ X. 'General type' is built from scratch and I checked the mathematics: rational m-pluricanonical forms live in (⋀^n Ω_{K(X)/K})^{⊗m}; on a nonempty affine open Spec A of a K-smooth scheme of relative dimension n, the K-span of a·⊗_i ⋀_j df_{ij} (a, f_ij ∈ A) is exactly the A-span, i.e. Γ(Spec A, ω^{⊗m}) embedded in the generic fibre (projective modules inject into their localisation); the infimum over nonempty affine opens is H^0(X', ω^{⊗m}) by gluing; `∃ c > 0, ∃ᶠ m, m^n ≤ c·P_m` is exactly κ = n by Iitaka's growth theorem; and 'X of general type ⇔ ∃ smooth proper integral X' birational to X with κ(X') = dim X'' is the textbook definition (well-defined by birational invariance of κ among smooth proper varieties). c03 was the runner-up (correct, adds proper + geometric integrality via pullback to the algebraic closure, matching the table's gloss), c04 is correct but heavier (stalk algebra + scalar-tower plumbing, explicit morphisms), c02 is correct but its intrinsic 'regular on every smooth affine model' definition relies on a subtler valuative-criterion/Hartogs argument and has two sorry'd tests. I accepted the deviation from the table's '(geometrically integral, projective)' gloss: over a number field an integral non-geometrically-integral variety has all K-points in the non-normal locus (so the conclusion holds trivially), and Zariski density of X(K) and being of general type are both birational invariants, so the statement over all integral varieties is equivalent to the projective one and matches the article's/Poonen's 'positive-dimensional variety of general type' wording literally.

context: In arithmetic geometry, the Bombieri–Lang conjecture is an unsolved problem conjectured by Enrico Bombieri and Serge Lang about the Zariski density of the set of rational points of an algebraic variety of general type.

decomposition_objections.text: None of substance. The table asks for (geometrically integral, projective) varieties; the file quantifies over integral separated finite-type K-schemes and defines general type through smooth *proper* birational models. Both deviations are equivalent to the table's reading (geometric integrality is automatic where K-points can be dense in characteristic 0; proper vs projective and singular vs smooth are absorbed by birational invariance of both Kodaira dimension and Zariski density of rational points), and they avoid primitives Mathlib lacks (projective morphisms, geometric integrality).

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Bombieri–Lang conjecture

The Bombieri–Lang conjecture predicts that the $K$-rational points of a positive-dimensional
variety of general type over a number field $K$ are not Zariski dense.

Mathlib has no notion of canonical bundle or Kodaira dimension, so this file defines "general
type" from scratch, following the classical description of pluricanonical forms as rational
differential forms. For an integral scheme $X$ over $K$ with function field $F = K(X)$, an
$m$-canonical rational form of degree $n$ is an element of
$(\bigwedge^n_F \Omega_{F/K})^{\otimes m}$. Such a form is regular on a nonempty affine open
$U = \operatorname{Spec} A$ if it is an $A$-linear combination of forms
$(df_{1,1} \wedge \dots \wedge df_{1,n}) \otimes \dots \otimes
(df_{m,1} \wedge \dots \wedge df_{m,n})$
with all $f_{i,j} \in A$. When $X$ is smooth of dimension $n$ over $K$, the forms regular on
every nonempty affine open are exactly the global sections $H^0(X, \omega_X^{\otimes m})$ of the
$m$-th power of the canonical bundle, and their $K$-dimension is the $m$-th plurigenus $P_m(X)$.
A smooth proper variety of dimension $n$ is of general type if its Kodaira dimension is $n$, i.e.
$P_m(X)$ grows like $m^n$. Kodaira dimension is a birational invariant of smooth proper
varieties, and a general variety is of general type if some (equivalently, every) smooth proper
variety birational to it is.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Bombieri–Lang conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombieri%E2%80%93Lang_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Kodaira dimension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kodaira_dimension)
- [La74] S. Lang, *Higher dimensional diophantine problems*, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 80 (1974),
  779–787.
- [Po12] B. Poonen, *Uniform boundedness of rational points and preperiodic points*,
  [arXiv:1206.7104](https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.7104).
- [DT15] P. Das, A. Turchet, *Rational Points, Rational Curves, and Entire Holomorphic Curves on
  Projective Varieties*, Contemp. Math. 654 (2015),
  [arXiv:1407.7750](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.7750).
-/

namespace BombieriLangConjecture

open CategoryTheory AlgebraicGeometry Filter
open scoped TensorProduct

universe u

variable (K : Type u) [Field K]

/-- The `K`-algebra structure on the function field $K(X)$ of an integral scheme `X` over
`Spec K`, induced by the structure morphism `X ⟶ Spec K`. -/
noncomputable scoped instance functionFieldAlgebra (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))]
    [IsIntegral X] : Algebra K X.functionField :=
  haveI : Nonempty (⊤ : X.Opens) := ⟨⟨genericPoint X, trivial⟩⟩
  ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of K)).inv ≫ (X ↘ Spec (.of K)).appTop ≫
    X.germToFunctionField ⊤).hom.toAlgebra

/-- The `K`-vector space $(\bigwedge^n_{K(X)} \Omega_{K(X)/K})^{\otimes m}$ of rational
`m`-canonical forms of degree `n` on an integral scheme `X` over `Spec K`, where $K(X)$ is
the function field of `X`. When `X` is smooth of dimension `n` over `K`, this is the generic
fibre of the `m`-th tensor power $\omega_X^{\otimes m}$ of the canonical bundle. -/
abbrev RationalPluricanonicalForm (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
    (n m : ℕ) : Type u :=
  ⨂[X.functionField]^m (⋀[X.functionField]^n Ω[X.functionField⁄K])

/-- The rational `m`-canonical forms of degree `n` on an integral scheme `X` over `Spec K`
that are *regular* on the nonempty open `U`, meaning that they are
$\Gamma(X, U)$-linear combinations of forms
$(df_{1,1} \wedge \dots \wedge df_{1,n}) \otimes \dots \otimes
(df_{m,1} \wedge \dots \wedge df_{m,n})$ with all $f_{i,j} \in \Gamma(X, U)$.
Since $K$ maps into $\Gamma(X, U)$, this $\Gamma(X, U)$-span is the same as the `K`-span of
the forms $a \cdot (df_{1,1} \wedge \dots \wedge df_{1,n}) \otimes \dots$ with
$a, f_{i,j} \in \Gamma(X, U)$.

This description is the correct one when `U` is affine and `X` is smooth of dimension `n`
over `K`: then it is the space of sections of $\omega_X^{\otimes m}$ over `U`. -/
noncomputable def regularPluricanonicalForms (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))]
    [IsIntegral X] (n m : ℕ) (U : X.Opens) [Nonempty U] :
    Submodule K (RationalPluricanonicalForm K X n m) :=
  Submodule.span K {ω | ∃ (a : Γ(X, U)) (f : Fin m → Fin n → Γ(X, U)),
    ω = algebraMap Γ(X, U) X.functionField a •
      ⨂ₜ[X.functionField] i, exteriorPower.ιMulti X.functionField n fun j ↦
        KaehlerDifferential.D K X.functionField (algebraMap Γ(X, U) X.functionField (f i j))}

/-- The rational `m`-canonical forms of degree `n` on an integral scheme `X` over `Spec K`
that are regular on every nonempty affine open of `X`. When `X` is smooth of dimension `n`
over `K`, this is the space of global sections $H^0(X, \omega_X^{\otimes m})$ of the `m`-th
tensor power of the canonical bundle $\omega_X = \bigwedge^n \Omega_{X/K}$. -/
noncomputable def globalPluricanonicalForms (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))]
    [IsIntegral X] (n m : ℕ) : Submodule K (RationalPluricanonicalForm K X n m) :=
  ⨅ (U : X.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen U) (_ : Nonempty U), regularPluricanonicalForms K X n m U

/-- The `m`-th *plurigenus* $P_m(X) = \dim_K H^0(X, \omega_X^{\otimes m})$ of an integral
scheme `X` over `Spec K`, computed with forms of degree `n`. This is the classical plurigenus
when `X` is smooth and proper of dimension `n` over `K` (in which case
$H^0(X, \omega_X^{\otimes m})$ is finite-dimensional). -/
noncomputable def plurigenus (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
    (n m : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Module.finrank K (globalPluricanonicalForms K X n m)

/-- A form that is regular on every nonempty affine open is regular on each of them. -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
lemma globalPluricanonicalForms_le (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
    (n m : ℕ) (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) [Nonempty U] :
    globalPluricanonicalForms K X n m ≤ regularPluricanonicalForms K X n m U :=
  iInf_le_of_le U (iInf_le_of_le hU (iInf_le _ ‹_›))

/-- Two schemes `X` and `Y` over `Spec K` are *birational* over `K` if they contain dense open
subschemes that are isomorphic as `K`-schemes. -/
def IsBirational (X Y : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of K))] : Prop :=
  ∃ (U : X.Opens) (V : Y.Opens) (e : (U : Scheme.{u}) ≅ V),
    Dense (U : Set X) ∧ Dense (V : Set Y) ∧
    (e.hom ≫ (V.ι ≫ (Y ↘ Spec (.of K)))) = (U.ι ≫ (X ↘ Spec (.of K)))

/-- Every scheme over `Spec K` is birational to itself. -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
lemma isBirational_refl (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))] : IsBirational K X X :=
  ⟨⊤, ⊤, Iso.refl _, by simp, by simp, by simp⟩

/-- A smooth proper integral scheme `X` of dimension `n` over `Spec K` is *of general type* if
its Kodaira dimension $\kappa(X)$ equals `n`, i.e. if its plurigenera $P_m(X)$ grow like
$m^n$: there is a constant $c > 0$ with $m^n \le c \cdot P_m(X)$ for infinitely many `m`.

(By Iitaka's theorem, $P_m(X) = O(m^{\kappa(X)})$, and $P_m(X) \ge a m^{\kappa(X)}$ for all
large `m` in the semigroup of `m` with $P_m(X) \ne 0$, so this is equivalent to
$\kappa(X) = n$.) -/
def IsSmoothProperOfGeneralType (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
    (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  IsProper (X ↘ Spec (.of K)) ∧ IsSmoothOfRelativeDimension n (X ↘ Spec (.of K)) ∧
    ∃ c : ℕ, 0 < c ∧ ∃ᶠ m in atTop, m ^ n ≤ c * plurigenus K X n m

/-- An integral scheme `X` over `Spec K` is *of general type* if it is birational over `K` to
a smooth proper integral `K`-scheme `X'` of some dimension `n` with Kodaira dimension
$\kappa(X') = n$. Since the Kodaira dimension is a birational invariant of smooth proper
varieties, the choice of `X'` does not matter. -/
def IsGeneralType (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))] : Prop :=
  ∃ (X' : Scheme.{u}) (_ : X'.Over (Spec (.of K))) (_ : IsIntegral X') (n : ℕ),
    IsBirational K X X' ∧ IsSmoothProperOfGeneralType K X' n

/-- A smooth proper integral `K`-scheme with Kodaira dimension equal to its dimension is of
general type. -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
lemma IsSmoothProperOfGeneralType.isGeneralType (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))]
    [IsIntegral X] {n : ℕ} (hX : IsSmoothProperOfGeneralType K X n) : IsGeneralType K X :=
  ⟨X, inferInstance, inferInstance, n, isBirational_refl K X, hX⟩

/-- The set of `K`-rational points of a scheme `X` over `Spec K`, viewed as a subset of the
underlying (Zariski) topological space of `X`: the images of the `K`-morphisms
`Spec K ⟶ X`. -/
def rationalPoints (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))] : Set X :=
  {x | ∃ p : Spec (.of K) ⟶ X, (p ≫ (X ↘ Spec (.of K))) = 𝟙 _ ∧ p.base default = x}

/-- The unique point of `Spec K` is `K`-rational. -/
@[category test, AMS 14]
lemma rationalPoints_spec : rationalPoints K (Spec (.of K)) = Set.univ :=
  Set.eq_univ_of_forall fun _ ↦ ⟨𝟙 _, by simp, Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩

/-- **Bombieri–Lang conjecture.** Let $K$ be a number field and let $X$ be a positive-dimensional
variety (an integral separated scheme of finite type over $K$) of general type over $K$. Then
the set $X(K)$ of $K$-rational points of $X$ is not dense in the Zariski topology on $X$.

The positive-dimensionality hypothesis excludes the point $\operatorname{Spec} K$, which is of
general type with trivially dense rational points. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11 14]
theorem bombieri_lang_conjecture [NumberField K] (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))]
    [IsIntegral X] [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of K))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of K))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of K))] (hdim : 0 < topologicalKrullDim X)
    (hX : IsGeneralType K X) :
    ¬ Dense (rationalPoints K X) := by
  sorry

end BombieriLangConjecture

items: 'Variety over K' is read as an integral, separated, quasi-compact, locally-of-finite-type scheme over Spec K (hypotheses [IsIntegral X] [IsSeparated] [QuasiCompact] [LocallyOfFiniteType] on X ↘ Spec (.of K)). Geometric integrality is NOT required: over a number field (char 0), an integral variety that is not geometrically integral has all K-points inside the non-normal locus, so the statement for integral varieties is equivalent to (and formally slightly stronger than) the one for geometrically integral varieties.

'General type' (`IsGeneralType K X`) is defined as: X is birational over K (dense open subschemes isomorphic as K-schemes, `IsBirational`) to some integral K-scheme X' that is proper, smooth of relative dimension n (Mathlib's `IsSmoothOfRelativeDimension`), and satisfies the Kodaira-dimension-n growth condition. This is the textbook convention (Kodaira dimension is a birational invariant of smooth proper varieties, and is defined for singular / non-proper varieties through a smooth proper model). Because Zariski density of K-points is also a birational invariant, this reading is equivalent to the standard smooth projective formulation.

'Proper' is used instead of 'projective' (Mathlib has no IsProjective morphism class). Over a field of characteristic 0, every smooth proper variety is birational to a smooth projective one (Chow + Hironaka), and plurigenera are birational invariants among smooth proper varieties, so this does not change the class of varieties of general type.

Pluricanonical forms are modelled concretely: an m-canonical rational form of degree n is an element of (⋀ⁿ_F Ω_{F/K})^{⊗m} for F = K(X) (Mathlib `KaehlerDifferential`, `exteriorPower`, `TensorPower`). A form is regular on a nonempty affine open U = Spec A iff it lies in the K-span (= A-span, since K maps into A) of forms a·(df₁₁∧…∧df₁ₙ)⊗…⊗(dfₘ₁∧…∧dfₘₙ) with a, f_{ij} ∈ A. For smooth X' of dimension n this is exactly Γ(U, ω_{X'}^{⊗m}) inside the generic fibre, and the intersection over all nonempty affine opens is H⁰(X', ω^{⊗m}) (sheaf gluing; sections of a locally free sheaf on an integral scheme inject into the generic fibre). Restricting to *affine* opens is essential (for non-affine U the A-span description is wrong).

Kodaira dimension = n is encoded by the growth condition ∃ c > 0, ∃ᶠ m in atTop, m^n ≤ c · P_m(X'), where P_m = Module.finrank K H⁰(X', ω^{⊗m}). By Iitaka's theorem P_m = O(m^κ) and P_m ≥ a·m^κ for large m in the semigroup {m : P_m ≠ 0}, so 'frequently' (limsup form) is exactly κ(X') = n; the 'eventually' form would also be equivalent (canonical bundle big ⇒ semigroup contains all large m) but needs an extra argument. finrank returns 0 for infinite-dimensional spaces, which cannot occur for proper X'.
The K-algebra structure on the function field K(X) is a scoped instance built from the structure morphism: K ≅ Γ(Spec K, ⊤) → Γ(X, ⊤) → K(X).

Rational points are the set {x : X | ∃ p : Spec K ⟶ X, p ≫ (X ↘ Spec K) = 𝟙 ∧ p.base default = x} of underlying points of K-morphisms; density is Mathlib's `Dense` in the underlying (Zariski) topological space of X.

'Positive-dimensional' (the article's general form) is encoded as 0 < topologicalKrullDim X, which for an integral finite-type K-scheme is the usual dimension; it excludes Spec K, which is of general type (κ = 0 = dim) with trivially dense rational points.
The number field K lives in the same universe as the scheme (`K : Type u`, `X : Scheme.{u}`), as required by `Spec (.of K)`.
Because FormalConjecturesForMathlib globally overloads `≫` as an asymptotic notation, categorical compositions in the file are fully parenthesised.

reviewer_notes: Omission reasons of c01/c05/c07/c08 (no canonical sheaf / Kodaira dimension in Mathlib) are legitimate concerns but overcautious: the pluricanonical spaces of a smooth variety over a field are faithfully describable inside the generic fibre (⋀^n Ω_{K(X)/K})^{⊗m} using Mathlib's Kähler differentials, exterior/tensor powers and the function field, as c02/c03/c04/c06 all did; none of these is a placeholder. Note the c03 report.json text does not match its file (the file requires proper + geometrically integral X; the report describes c06's hypotheses) — I judged on the Lean text. Ambiguities in the original: 'variety' (integral vs geometrically integral, projective or not) — all readings are equivalent for this conjecture, see per-slot; the 'weak' surface form and 'refined' finiteness form from the article are not posed by the list entry and were not stated. Positive-dimensionality is imposed (0 < topologicalKrullDim X) since a point is of general type with dense rational points.
